title: Grade 3 Life Skills — Spending, Saving, and Planning
subject: General Knowledge and Life Skills
description: Practice with questions on budget, goals, needs, wants, price.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What is saving money?
choices: setting money aside to use later

questions.question: What is a spending plan often called?
Which is usually a basic need?
You have $8 and spend $3. How much remains?
You save $2 each week for four weeks. How much did you save?
Which receipt detail helps check what you paid?
Which is a short-term saving goal?
choices: buying a $6 book in three weeks

questions.question: You have $10. A toy costs $7 and a book costs $5. What choice fits your budget?
What is an example of income?
choices: a jar that holds no money
a toy price on a shelf
money earned for doing an agreed job

questions.question: What is an expense?
choices: a gift placed in your savings jar
the number of items on a shelf

questions.question: Why compare prices for the same item?
choices: to find an option that costs less
to make identical items different sizes
to make all stores use one logo

questions.question: A poster costs $9 and you have $6 saved. How much more do you need?
You choose to pay for a ball with your spare money instead of stickers. What did you give up?
choices: the stickers you could have bought

questions.question: Which choice keeps a useful record of spending?
choices: write down the amount each time you buy something
record only the store's wall color

questions.question: You plan to spend $10. Item A costs $4 and item B costs $3. How much of the plan is left after both?
What is a reason to set aside money you do not need to spend now?
choices: it makes prices the same everywhere
it guarantees every purchase is free
it can help pay for a future need or goal
it changes a store's price immediately

questions.question: Which choice can help you buy only what you planned?
choices: choose the most expensive item first
make a list and check prices before paying
add every colorful item to the cart

questions.question: Two pens of the same type are $1 each at one shop and $3 for two at another. Which costs less for two?
Your change is $2 less than expected. What is a good first step?
choices: check the receipt and count the change calmly

questions.question: Which shows a plan that covers a future goal first?
choices: set aside the planned savings before spending what is left
spend all the money and then write a savings goal
buy a second item before checking the price
